Relative to hard voting alone [33], S_MAC provides a continuous ranking score, allowing variants with the same vote count or categorical output to be prioritised for expert review and functional follow-up. The four thresholded learner decisions define the V0–V4 audit states, whereas S_MAC, obtained through logistic meta-calibration of Mean4, is reported alongside the vote pattern and neither contributes an additional vote nor alters the shared vote-state descriptor. This dual-output design keeps learner-level disagreement visible while adding ranking resolution beyond vote count alone. Because S_MAC was calibrated within the HBOCpred anchor framework, it is not a clinical posterior probability or a direct PP3/BP4 evidence threshold [18,19,34].

Two forms of predictor–label dependence limit interpretation. First, some eligible and retained meta-predictors were trained partly on clinical variant resources that may overlap the anchor labels; excluding a variant from HBOCpred training does not exclude it from upstream training. Second, computational evidence can contribute to the clinical classifications later used as reference labels through PP3/BP4. Newly sampled classifications can still contain such computational evidence. The available source data do not identify which evidence determined each classification, so its contribution cannot be quantified. Removing BayesDel addAF and AlphaMissense did not materially reduce first-repeat discrimination, but other frequency-informed and clinically trained predictors remained; the experiment is neither frequency-free validation nor a demonstration that circularity has been removed.

The development and application populations also differ in ascertainment. Variants with decisive evidence are more likely to have definite source classifications, whereas the intended application population remains unresolved. The 19 shifted predictors and 2.70-fold increase in mixed votes are compatible with this selection mechanism, although they do not prove its causal contribution. They make direct transfer of internal estimates to unresolved variants unjustified; the magnitude and even gene-specific pattern of miscalibration or error cannot be estimated without application reference outcomes. The substantial recoverability of gene identity and the FANCA and NBN holdout findings further show why the pooled AUROC cannot support uniform claims across genes. Ancestry-specific error and demographic fairness were not assessable because those data were unavailable.

The asymmetric opposite-direction counts are clinically relevant to interpretation: 32/973 LP/P anchors received V0, compared with 16/1,187 B/LB anchors receiving V4. A low pathogenic-direction score could therefore deprioritise a truly pathogenic variant. We removed predicted-B/LB clinical-sounding output labels and explicitly prohibit using V0 to exclude a variant from expert review or to justify reassurance. Renaming the output does not remove this risk. The equal-cost balanced-accuracy threshold objective was not optimised for cancer-predisposition decision costs; a clinically cost-sensitive operating point would require independent development and evaluation.

Annotation quality and transcript scope impose additional limits. The original development sheet does not preserve every historical transcript/consequence pairing, and 40 anchors lack a current same-gene missense annotation. The current-transcript missense refit is reassuring only as an internal sensitivity check; it does not repair the original curation provenance. Multi-valued predictor fields were resolved by the first finite numeric token, which cannot establish transcript-specific alignment across tools. Furthermore, 114 source anchors could not receive an output under the completeness rule, including the entire NR group. Reliability_index was excluded from the primary candidate set because it is annotation metadata rather than direct biological evidence, but ascertainment information can remain encoded in predictor availability and values.

The externally sourced records do not establish independent clinical validity. A well-curated common-variant set can test behaviour on a selected benign-enriched stratum, but choosing it by allele frequency limits independence from frequency-informed predictors and does not represent rare uncertain missense variants. Conversely, long-documented pathogenic alleles can overlap upstream training resources. Two class-specific sources need not originate in one database, but combining their counts would confound class with source and would not yield transportable accuracy or predictive values. A future evaluation should freeze the entire pipeline and reporting convention, document transcript-aligned inputs and upstream overlap, and use independently adjudicated functional, segregation or case–control evidence where possible across both classes and genes. These analyses cannot remove computational evidence from the source labels or establish representativeness of the unresolved population.

HBOCpred offers an auditable way to organise computational evidence for research review of unresolved germline missense variants. A shared descriptor reports unanimous B/LB-directed votes, mixed votes or unanimous LP/P-directed votes, while exact V-state and S_MAC preserve disagreement and ranking information. The internal results are source-label consistency estimates with explicit completeness and per-gene limitations. Independent evidence is required before these outputs can support clinical reclassification, exclusion from review or patient management.
new_text:
Relative to hard voting alone [33], S_MAC distinguishes variants with the same vote count for expert review and functional follow-up. The four learner decisions define V0–V4; S_MAC ranks variants without adding a vote or changing their descriptor. Its calibration against source labels does not provide a clinical probability or a PP3/BP4 evidence threshold [18,19,34].

Agreement with ClinVar reflects two sources of shared information. Some constituent predictors were trained on clinical variant classifications, and ClinVar submitters may use computational evidence through PP3/BP4. A variant held out of HBOCpred can therefore remain linked to predictor training or to labels informed by similar tools. Removing BayesDel addAF and AlphaMissense left internal discrimination largely unchanged, while other clinically trained or frequency-informed predictors remained. The external lists face related limits: common gnomAD variants were selected by frequency, and long-documented hospital alleles may overlap upstream training. These records support an audit of selected variants; they do not provide an independent test of clinical accuracy.

Nineteen predictors shifted between anchors and unresolved variants, and mixed votes were 2.70 times as frequent in the application catalogue. This pattern is consistent with definite classifications being more common when the available evidence is decisive. Reference outcomes are needed to measure performance in the unresolved population. Gene identity was also recoverable from the predictors with 89.40% accuracy. The lower held-out sensitivity in FANCA and the small NBN stratum show why the pooled AUROC should be read alongside the per-gene results.

V0 included 32 of 973 LP/P anchors, whereas V4 included 16 of 1,187 B/LB anchors. This asymmetry matters because low scores could delay review of pathogenic variants. V0 must therefore remain a model-direction descriptor, never a reason to exclude a variant from expert review or reassure a patient. Our balanced-accuracy threshold objective weighted the two classes equally; clinical decision costs require separate evaluation.

Missing annotations were concentrated in the least documented records: 101 of the 114 incomplete anchors belonged to the NR group. Reliability_index was excluded because it describes annotation quality; the completeness audit documents the imbalance that remains across records. Forty anchors also lacked a current same-gene missense annotation, and historical transcript assignments remain incomplete despite the transcript-restricted sensitivity analysis. The next evaluation should use a frozen pipeline, matched transcripts and independently assessed functional, segregation or case–control evidence across genes and both classes. HBOCpred’s present role is to organise variants for research review and functional follow-up.
